title: Beatrix and the Uniform
premise: In 1889, apprentice clockmaker Felix Whitlock is summoned to the Royal Observatory to repair its failing master clock, a job meant to keep him safely anonymous. There he meets Beatrix Calloway, an archivist who recognizes the handwriting on a stranger's letter as that of her brother Edmund—declared dead at sea three years ago—and the handwriting belongs to Felix's own master, who taught Felix to forge it. As Felix repairs the clock, he uncovers his master's role in falsifying Edmund's death to protect a smuggling ring, forcing him to choose between loyalty to the man who raised him and truth for the woman he has come to love. In the end, Felix testifies before the Admiralty, the workshop is seized but its ledgers preserved by Beatrix, and the two of them open a small repair shop together where time, finally, belongs to them.
about_author: M. M. Vasquez is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring Victorian scientific instruments before turning to fiction. They write historical novels about people whose quiet trades collide with history's loud machinery.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Felix Whitlock, POV. Summoned from his master's cramped workshop to the observatory, Felix carries tools and a lifetime habit of being unnoticed. The master clock's failure threatens Greenwich time itself. Emotional beat: anxious pride—the first solo commission of his life, shadowed by his master's strange reluctance to let him go.

chapters.title: A Stranger with a Letter
chapters.summary: Beatrix Calloway, POV. Archivist Beatrix intercepts a courier delivering sealed instructions to the observatory and freezes: the handwriting is her drowned brother Edmund's. She confronts the courier, learns nothing, but pockets a discarded envelope. Emotional beat: grief reignited into obsession; the dead do not write letters.

chapters.title: Gears and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Working inside the clock tower, Felix notices Beatrix watching him, cataloguing everything. Their first real conversation reveals she suspects the observatory's records were altered around the date of her brother's death. Emotional beat: wary attraction; two careful people circling the same secret from opposite sides.

chapters.title: The Hand I Know
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Beatrix shows Felix the letter, asking if the workshop could authenticate it. Felix recognizes his master's hand instantly—he was trained to copy it—and lies badly. Emotional beat: guilt's first bite; Felix realizes invisibility now costs someone else the truth.

chapters.title: What Master Marlow Kept
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Returning home, Felix searches the workshop and finds Edmund's sea chest hidden beneath the floorboards—alive, then. His master catches him, confesses only fragments: debts, threats, a name. Emotional beat: shattered loyalty; the father-figure becomes a suspect, and Felix must decide what to carry back to Greenwich.

chapters.title: Uniforms
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Beatrix wears borrowed observatory livery to access restricted logs and discovers Edmund's death certificate predates the storm that supposedly killed him. She is nearly caught by the astronomer's clerk. Emotional beat: defiance sharpening into danger; identity as armor and as risk.

chapters.title: The Escapement
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. The master clock nears completion as Felix finds proof his master forged the death notice under coercion from the smuggling ring still operating through the docks. He and Beatrix compare findings and admit their feelings in the tower's dark. Emotional beat: tenderness under deadline; love declared while the evidence mounts against everyone they care about.

chapters.title: Fire Watch
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The ring, alerted, sets fire to the workshop to destroy the ledgers. Felix races in after them; Beatrix pulls him out half-suffocated, clutching one salvaged ledger. Emotional beat: terror and sacrifice; what survives the flames is exactly enough to condemn or to save.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Before the Admiralty, Felix testifies to the forgery, naming his master and exposing the ring; his master, broken, corroborates and reveals Edmund lives in hiding abroad. Emotional beat: catharsis at cost; truth spoken aloud ends Felix's invisibility forever, and he no longer wants it back.

chapters.title: Keeping Time
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Months later, Beatrix and Felix open a small repair shop; a letter arrives in Edmund's own hand, promising reunion. The observatory's clock, restored, strikes the hour across the river. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; loyalty survived its trial, truth set them both free, and time is finally theirs to keep.
